features.feature: Sequential stages and direct executable steps
Persistent build history and stage/step state
Retry completed builds with preserved parameters
features.notes: A retry creates a new build and reuses persisted non-secret parameters; secret parameters require explicit replacement values, while richer retry policies and attempt grouping remain planned.

features.feature: FIFO queue with global and per-project limits
features.notes: Queued cancellation is handled before execution; priority, resource requirements, and observable queue administration remain planned.

features.feature: Build artifact collection, checksums, and download
features.notes: Local workspace artifacts are copied into build-scoped storage and exposed through the API. Remote agents package declared matches into bounded checksum-verified chunks before the server validates and stores them; retention policies and remote object stores remain planned.
Validated locally on Unix; remote agents and container execution are planned.

Exact relative cache paths are validated, entries are isolated by project and key, restored before execution, and saved atomically after success; fallback keys, eviction, and remote backends remain planned.

Container declarations validate an image and assemble a direct docker run command with a bounded workspace mount, separated arguments, timeout propagation, and automatic removal; Docker runtime execution, image policy, and end-to-end artifact/cancellation behavior remain unverified locally.

A versioned, non-executing analyzer reports line-level supported, partial, and unsupported findings, exposes them through the headless API and desktop report, and can generate a valid draft for simple quoted sh/bat steps; full Groovy/plugin interpretation and broad generated Rivetfile conversion remain planned.

Explicit local fetch, detached revision checkout, and clean preparation are supported at build admission. A provider-neutral credential ID can resolve through Rivet's encrypted local vault and reach Git through ephemeral HTTP Basic configuration; signed GitHub and GitLab push adapters can feed the same build admission path with an explicit project route. Credential lifecycle and broader provider event mapping remain planned.

features.feature: Manual/API builds and persistent UTC cron schedules
features.notes: Five-field cron expressions are validated, persisted, atomically claimed, dispatched into real builds, and exposed through API, CLI, and desktop controls; pull-request, broader repository-event, and upstream trigger mapping remain planned.

The generic endpoint verifies HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body, atomically deduplicates event IDs, and queues one real build; provider adapters are tracked separately and broader repository-event mapping remains planned.

features.feature: Signed GitHub and GitLab push adapters
features.notes: Explicit project routes normalize GitHub push deliveries and GitLab Push Hook/Tag Push Hook deliveries into the common idempotent build path. GitHub HMAC-SHA256 and GitLab signed webhook headers are verified over the raw body, optional fetch credential IDs are attached, and stale/invalid messages are rejected; pull requests and broader provider event coverage remain planned.

features.feature: Versioned agent registration, assignment, and remote execution
features.notes: Agents negotiate a versioned protocol, advertise capabilities, reconnect with bounded backoff and session fencing, appear online or stale, and match only when capability and available executor requirements pass through POST /api/v1/agents/match. Remote builds reserve matching capacity, transfer bounded workspaces and declared artifact bundles, execute through the shared Rust runner, relay typed events and output, and propagate cancellation. A disconnect gets at most one replacement-agent attempt; unavailable recovery closes unfinished work as failed. Rivetfile steps still require identical requirements within one remote build; durable restart recovery, exactly-once semantics, and richer retry policy remain planned.

Optional in-memory Bearer-token protection, mandatory authentication for non-loopback binds, exact CORS origins, request limits, baseline security headers, and a private policy file with digest-backed roles, project-scoped route authorization, and local token creation/listing/revocation are supported; user accounts, sessions, expiration, audit history, and external identity providers remain planned.

features.feature: Secret parameter redaction and log masking
features.notes: Secret parameters require runtime input without defaults, are redacted in persisted build/API data, masked in emitted process output, and must be supplied again for retries. SCM credentials can be stored as authenticated ciphertext in a passphrase-encrypted local vault and referenced by ID; credential ownership, rotation, keychain integration, and project access control remain planned.

The CLI reads a passphrase and secret from private regular files, stores only authenticated ciphertext, lists metadata without secrets, and the server resolves non-secret IDs for Git fetches. Keychain-backed storage, rotation, audit ownership, and project-level access control remain planned.
Rivet will define a versioned extension protocol instead of reproducing the Java plugin ABI.

Manifests, explicit permissions, bounded length-prefixed JSON frames, a direct-argument subprocess host, bounded local catalog discovery/API, and a desktop model are present. Permission enforcement in a lifecycle manager, WASM execution, and lifecycle management remain planned.
